# Run book: See the queue channels and received messages

[Run books](README.md) | [User guide](../user-guide/watch-the-queues.md) | [Spec](../specs/watch-the-queues.md)

## Contents

- [Purpose](#purpose)

## Purpose

See the configured channels without opening configuration files, and watch what the handler receives.

## Preconditions

- The example API is running.

## Verify

Automatically: `npx playwright test e2e/journeys.spec.ts -g "See the queue channels and received messages"` (add `E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8088` to run against the compose stack).

By hand, in the example web application at `/messaging/queues`:

1. **Read the configured channels.** The table lists each channel with its provider, queue, host and whether the receiver is on. Connection strings are never shown. Expect: The channel table lists the provider and queue.
2. **Look at the received messages.** The list shows the last messages this host received, newest first. Refresh to update it. Expect: A received message is listed with its time and text.

## Troubleshooting

**Table 1 — Known problems**

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Received list stays empty | The channel has DisableReceiver set, or nothing was sent | Enable the receiver in the MessageQueue section and send a message |

Related framework features: OoBDev.MessageQueueing; OoBDev.RabbitMq, OoBDev.Microsoft.Azure.StorageAccount.
